method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Manage a burn as trauma**, prioritising burns first aid. **Accurate TBSA drives the fluid decision — and TBSA excludes epidermal burns.**
claims.source_text: Burn injuries should be managed as a trauma case with prioritisation of appropriate burns first aid Accurate total body surface area (TBSA) estimation is essential for fluid resuscitation decision making. TBSA does not include epidermal burns
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Primary survey first — do not get distracted by the burn.**
claims.source_text: Like all traumas, paediatric burn assessments require a primary and secondary survey with the initial aim of identifying and managing immediate life threats. Do not get distracted by the burn injury
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Airway burn/inhalation signs** — stridor, hoarseness, black sputum, respiratory distress, singed nasal hairs, facial swelling, soot in the mouth, intraoral oedema, significant neck burn: **consider early intubation.** Suspected airway burn or carbon monoxide: **high-flow oxygen.**
claims.source_text: Signs of airway burn/inhalation injury: stridor, hoarseness, black sputum, respiratory distress, singed nasal hairs or facial swelling Sign of oropharyngeal burn: soot in mouth, intraoral oedema and erythema Significant neck burn: circumferential, or oedema leading to airway compromise If above present, consider early intubation If suspicion of airway burns or carbon monoxide intoxication apply high flow oxygen
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Full-thickness or circumferential chest/abdominal wall burns with abnormal breathing: consider escharotomy** — needs the tertiary burns service.
claims.source_text: If abnormal with chest wall or abdominal wall full thickness and/or circumferential burns, consider escharotomy - this will require referral to tertiary burns service
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Early shock — look for a cause other than the burn.** Ideally 2 points of IV/IO access; bolus for haemodynamic instability; **IV fluid if over 10% TBSA**, rate by the modified Parkland formula.
claims.source_text: If early shock is present, consider causes other than the burn Ideally obtain 2 points of IV/intraosseous access Give IV fluid bolus in setting of haemodynamic instability Give IV fluid if >10% TBSA using modified parkland formula for rate calculation
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Remove clothing, nappy and jewellery** in contact with the burn and distal to it. **Cool as soon as possible (within 3 hours) for a total of 20 minutes with cool running water.**
claims.source_text: Remove clothing, nappy, and jewellery in contact with burn source and distal to the burn Cool affected area as soon as possible (within 3 hours from time of burn) for total of 20 minutes with cool running water
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Never apply ice; avoid hydrogel burn products.** Cooling may be paused for hypothermia or significant distress.
claims.source_text: Never apply ice and avoid use of hydrogel burn products Cooling can be paused to prevent hypothermia and for significant distress, continue when clinically appropriate
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cling film lengthways — never wrapped circumferentially, and not on the face or a chemical burn.** Paraffin ointment for facial burns.
claims.source_text: Cover burn with plastic cling film lengthways along the burn Do not wrap circumferentially Do not apply plastic cling film to face or chemical burn Use paraffin ointment on facial burns
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Prevent hypothermia:** remove wet clothes and dressings after cooling, cover the wound and child, warm the room or use warming devices, consider warm IV fluids.
claims.source_text: Prevent hypothermia Remove wet clothes/dressings after initial cooling Try to keep child otherwise warm Cover the wound and the child after assessment When possible warm the environment or use warming devices Consider warm intravenous fluids
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Chemical burns: discuss decontamination with Poisons Information, 131126.**
claims.source_text: Discuss chemical burn decontamination with Poisons Information, phone 131126
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider child abuse:** immersion scalds, patterned contact burns, a mechanism that does not fit the pattern, burns on the back or genitalia. Check tetanus status.
claims.source_text: Consider child abuse Look for pattern of burn and/or inconsistent history eg immersion scald burns, patterned burn by hot object, mechanism not in keeping with pattern of burn, location of burn, eg back or genitalia Tetanus immunisation status
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Analgesia early and throughout, especially for dressings and mobilisation. Procedural sedation is recommended for debridement and dressings.**
claims.source_text: Ensure adequate pain relief on presentation and ongoing analgesia, especially during dressings and mobilisation … Procedural sedation is recommended for debridement and dressings.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Depth is hard to judge in the first 48–72 hours.** Do not count erythema-only (epidermal) areas.
claims.source_text: Burns are dynamic wounds, it is difficult to accurately estimate the true depth and extent of the wound in the first 48-72 hours Do not include area with epidermal burn (erythema only)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Depth by appearance:** epidermal — red, no blisters, brisk refill, sensation present · superficial dermal — pale pink, blisters, brisk, painful · mid dermal — dark pink, blisters, sluggish, ± sensation · deep dermal — blotchy red, ± blisters, refill and sensation absent · full thickness — white, no blisters, refill and sensation absent.
claims.source_text: Classification Depth Colour Blisters Capillary refill Sensation Superficial Epidermal Red No Brisk Present Superficial dermal Pale pink Present Brisk Painful Mid dermal Dark pink Present Sluggish +/- Deep Deep dermal Blotchy red +/- Absent Absent Full thickness White No Absent Absent
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Baseline tests:** major burn (≥10% TBSA) — Hb, electrolytes, BGL, group and hold, VBG · suspected inhalation — VBG for CO or cyanide · electrical — ECG.
claims.source_text: Major burn (≥10% TBSA) Haemoglobin, electrolytes, BGL, group and hold, VBG … Suspected inhalation injury VBG for carbon monoxide or hydrogen cyanide poisoning Electrical burn ECG
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Count from the time of the burn, not presentation.** Resuscitation fluid is **Hartmann's**, with maintenance **sodium chloride 0.9% + glucose 5% through a separate line**; volume by the Modified Parkland Formula.
claims.source_text: Acute fluid management in burns ≥10% TBSA … Calculate requirements from time of the burn, not from time of presentation Give resuscitation fluids (Hartmann's solution) and, via a separate line, maintenance fluids (sodium chloride 0.9% with glucose 5%) Calculate resuscitation fluid volume using Modified Parkland Formula
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give half in the first 8 hours, the rest over the next 16.** Review the rate every 1–2 hours against urine output and fluid state — the total is an estimate. **Hartmann's is first choice; sodium chloride 0.9% if unavailable.**
claims.source_text: Give half the total amount of the first 8 hours then the remainder over the next 16 hours Review fluid rate every 1-2 hours and adjust rate according to the urine output and fluid state, total resuscitation fluid volume is estimate and must be individually tailored Hartmann's solution is the fluid of choice - if unavailable, use sodium chloride 0.9%
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Urinary catheter; nil by mouth with a nasogastric tube** (risk of ileus). Delayed resuscitation, electrical and inhalation injury need more fluid — discuss with the specialist team.
claims.source_text: Insert urinary catheter for strict fluid balance Keep nil by mouth and insert nasogastric tube, gastric ileus is a potential complication Patients with delayed fluid resuscitation, electrical conduction injury and inhalation injury have higher fluid requirements. Discuss with specialist team
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **De-roof blisters over 5 mm or crossing a joint.**
claims.source_text: De-roof blisters >5mm or if crossing joint with moist gauze or forceps and scissors.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Facial burns: fluorescein 2% for corneal damage.** Ocular burns: irrigate at least 30 minutes with sodium chloride 0.9%, topical chloramphenicol, **urgent ophthalmology review.** Alkali eye injury may need 2–4 hours of irrigation, until pain stops and eye pH is 7.0–7.2.
claims.source_text: All facial burns should have assessment with fluorescein 2% eye drops to assess for corneal damage Irrigate for at least 30 minutes with sodium chloride 0.9%. … Topical chloramphenicol to prevent secondary infection Urgent ophthalmology review … Alkaline injury, may require between 2-4 hours of continuous irrigation (continue until pain stops) and eye pH is 7.0-7.2
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suspected carbon monoxide or cyanide poisoning: 100% oxygen**, and liaise early with the burns unit, ICU and Poisons Information.
claims.source_text: Suspicion of associated carbon monoxide (CO) poisoning, Cyanide poisoning Liaise early with paediatric burn unit, ICU and Poisons Information, phone 131126 Apply 100% oxygen
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Electrical injury:** involve the burns service and ICU early; look for entry/exit wounds; consider spinal precautions and **24-hour ECG monitoring**; monitor CK and urine haemoglobin.
claims.source_text: Electrical injuries Liaise early with Paediatric Burn Service and Intensive Care Ensure documented history of domestic/low voltage AC, high voltage DC or lightening Inspect for entrance/exit wounds Consider spinal precautions Risk of dysrhythmias, consider 24 hours ECG monitoring Monitor for elevated CK, urine haemoglobin and haemochromogen
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Discuss with the state paediatric burns service** for: over 5% TBSA · over 5% full thickness · face, ears, eyes, neck, hands, feet, genitalia, perineum or a major joint even if under 5% · any inhalation injury · circumferential · chemical or electrical · associated trauma or spinal injury · **under 12 months** · suspected abuse.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local state paediatric burns service when … Complex burns >5% TBSA >5% full thickness burn Special areas: face, ears, eyes, neck, hands, feet, genitalia, perineum or a major joint, even if <5% All inhalation/airway injuries Circumferential burn Chemical / electrical mechanism Associated with trauma and/or spinal cord injury Children <12 months Suspected child abuse
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the local paediatric team** for suspected abuse or self-inflicted burn, multiple co-morbidities, or doubt about caring for the burn at home.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team when Suspected child abuse or self-inflicted burn Multiple co-morbidities Concern regarding ability to care for burns at home
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - acute management' (Last updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns/, retrieved 2026-09-23
